subtopics.title: Policy Overview and Targets
subtopics.summary: Delhi EV Policy 2.0 was notified by the Government of NCT of Delhi and is scheduled to come into force from 1 July 2026, remaining effective until 31 March 2030. It builds upon the achievements of Delhi EV Policy 2020 and aims to turn Delhi into a leading electric mobility hub. The policy targets at least 30% electrification of Delhi's total vehicle fleet by 31 March 2030, with a focus on high-usage and high-emission transport segments.

subtopics.title: Registration Rules and Phase-out
subtopics.summary: New registrations in Delhi move to electric models in stages. From 1 January 2027 only electric 3-wheelers and electric N1 category light commercial trucks can be newly registered, and from 1 April 2028 new 2-wheeler registrations are restricted to electric models. Existing petrol and diesel vehicles may keep operating until the end of their prescribed service life. Schools must also electrify part of their bus fleets.

subtopics.title: Investment, Support and Charging
subtopics.summary: The policy plans total investment of approximately 15,000 crore. Government support is restricted exclusively to battery electric vehicles and not to hybrid vehicles. The plan includes installing over 30,000 public charging stations across Delhi. Financial support and investment is handled by the Delhi Transport Department, and infrastructure development by Delhi Transco Limited.

subtopics.title: National Schemes: NEMMP, FAME and PM E-DRIVE
subtopics.summary: Delhi's policy sits within national electric mobility efforts. The National Electric Mobility Mission Plan was launched in 2013, and the government committed to achieve 30% e-mobility by 2030. FAME India, launched by the Ministry of Heavy Industries & Public Enterprises, is part of that mission plan and offers subsidies for several vehicle types. PM E-DRIVE, launched in 2024 with the Ministry of Heavy Industries as nodal ministry, builds on FAME-II and the Electric Mobility Promotion Scheme 2024.

quizzes.title: Delhi EV Policy 2.0 Overview Quiz
quizzes.passage: The Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi has notified the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy 2.0, which is scheduled to come into force from 1 July 2026. The policy will remain effective until 31 March 2030. It builds upon the achievements of the Delhi EV Policy 2020 and provides a comprehensive roadmap for transforming Delhi into a leading electric mobility hub. A central aim is to reduce vehicular emissions by encouraging the electrification of high-usage and high-emission transport segments. The policy sets an electrification target of at least 30 per cent of Delhi's total vehicle fleet by 31 March 2030. Several segments have been identified as priorities, including two-wheelers, three-wheelers, commercial goods carriers, school buses, app-based aggregator fleets and government-owned transport fleets. The policy also seeks to promote the widespread adoption of zero-emission vehicles, reduce urban air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions, and encourage sustainable public and commercial transport. It is linked to India's clean energy and climate commitments. The idea of electric mobility is not new in India. The National Electric Mobility Mission Plan, launched in 2013, set out an earlier national plan to expand the number of electric vehicles on the roads. Delhi's policy therefore sits within a longer national effort to shift transport away from petrol and diesel vehicles.

quizzes.title: Registration Rules Recall
quizzes.passage: Delhi's electric vehicle policy changes which new vehicles can be registered in the city, and it does so in stages rather than all at once. The first categories affected are electric three-wheelers and light commercial trucks, while two-wheelers come later in the schedule. Schools are also covered by the transition. Their bus fleets must include a growing share of electric buses, and the policy sets a longer-term goal for the whole school bus fleet. School buses are one of several priority segments, which also include commercial goods carriers, app-based aggregator fleets and government-owned transport fleets. The policy's wider objective is to reduce urban air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. It also aims to encourage sustainable public and commercial transport across the city. Together, the registration rules and school bus targets show how the policy moves Delhi towards electric mobility over the period up to 2030. The policy is notified by the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi and comes into force from 1 July 2026. Demand for petrol and diesel is expected to reduce, and new jobs are expected to be created in the automobile sector. Reduction in pollution-induced health problems is also listed as a benefit. The booklet lists these as expected benefits of the shift towards electric vehicles.
